provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Revision of jss two work
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to recall basic skills learned in JSS two, list health topics covered previously, and demonstrate proper warm-up techniques.
Introduction:
We have learned many skills in JSS two and this week we will revise them to prepare for new topics. This revision will help us remember important knowledge.
Content:
We will review athletics skills like running and jumping techniques. We will also revisit health topics including hygiene and nutrition. For example, we will discuss how eating akara and bread for breakfast gives energy for school. We will practice warm-up exercises like stretching and jogging as done before physical education classes.
Class activity:
Students will form groups and demonstrate one skill each learned in JSS two, while others watch and identify the skill being performed.
Evaluation questions:
1. Name two skills learned in JSS two PE class.
2. Why is warming up important before exercise?
3. How does good nutrition help in sports?
4. What health topic did you find most interesting last term?
Summary:
This week we revised important skills and health topics from JSS two to build a strong foundation for this term's lessons.

topics.title: Athletics: throws
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate proper throwing techniques for shot put and javelin, explain safety rules for throwing events, and identify common errors in throwing form.
Introduction:
Last term we learned basic running and jumping skills. Today we will learn throwing skills which are important parts of athletics competitions like the National Sports Festival.
Content:
Shot put is a throwing event where you push a heavy metal ball. Hold the shot put at your neck with fingers spread, then twist your body and push forward. Javelin throwing involves gripping the thin metal spear near the tail, running forward, and throwing over your shoulder. Safety rules include throwing only when the area is clear and never turning back to see where the implement lands. We practice with soft javelins first before using real ones.
Class activity:
Students will practice shot put technique using soft balls and javelin throwing using foam javelins in the school field, taking turns and observing each other's form.
Evaluation questions:
1. Describe the proper grip for shot put.
2. What safety rule must be followed during javelin throwing?
3. Name two body parts that should move when throwing shot put.
4. Why do we start with foam implements before using real ones?
Summary:
Today we learned proper techniques for shot put and javelin throwing, which are important skills for athletics competitions.

topics.title: Athletics: jumps
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate high jump technique, explain the approach and takeoff phases, and identify common faults in jumping performance.
Introduction:
After learning throwing events last week, we now focus on jumping events in athletics. High jump is one of the most exciting events in sports days like our inter-house sports competition.
Content:
The high jump technique has three main parts: approach, takeoff, and clearance. For approach, run diagonally toward the mat with increasing speed. At takeoff, push off the takeoff foot while swinging the lead leg upward. For clearance, arch your body over the bar with your back facing the ground. Common faults include jumping too early or not high enough. We practice using low heights first and gradually increase as skills improve. Like when children jump over a rope during break time, we start small and build up.
Class activity:
Students will practice high jump technique using a crossbar starting at low height, with classmates taking turns and providing feedback on form.
Evaluation questions:
1. Name the three phases of high jump technique.
2. What is the proper body position during clearance?
3. Why do we start with low heights when learning high jump?
4. What happens if you jump too early in the approach?
Summary:
We have learned the proper technique for high jump which consists of approach, takeoff, and clearance phases.

topics.title: Ball games: football
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate basic football skills like dribbling and passing, explain simple tactics in football, and participate in a controlled football match.
Introduction:
Today we start learning football skills, which is Nigeria's most popular sport played everywhere from school fields to neighborhood streets during weekends.
Content:
Football skills include dribbling (moving with the ball at your feet), passing (kicking the ball to teammates), and shooting (kicking the ball toward the goal). Dribbling is done by tapping the ball lightly with your foot while running. Passing can be done with the inside of your foot for accuracy. Simple tactics include spreading out on the field to create space and supporting teammates with the ball. Like how traders spread their wares at the market, players should spread across the field to find space. We practice these skills in drills before playing a match.
Class activity:
Students will practice dribbling around cones and passing to partners, then participate in a small-sided football match applying the skills learned.
Evaluation questions:
1. What part of the foot is best used for accurate passing?
2. Name two basic football skills.
3. Why is spreading out important in football?
4. How is football played differently on a street compared to a proper field?
Summary:
We have learned basic football skills and simple tactics that help in playing the game effectively.

topics.title: Ball games: basketball
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate proper shooting technique, explain basic rules of basketball, and participate in a basketball game using learned skills.
Introduction:
After football last week, we now learn basketball skills which is played in many Nigerian schools and requires different techniques but similar teamwork.
Content:
Basketball shooting involves holding the ball with both hands, elbows bent, and releasing toward the basket with a follow-through. The shooting hand faces the basket while the guiding hand is on the side. Basic rules include dribbling (bouncing the ball while moving), passing, and shooting without traveling (taking steps without dribbling). Like how market women balance their trays while walking, players must balance the ball while moving. We practice shooting drills first, then passing, before playing a game. The game is played with two teams trying to score by throwing the ball through the opponent's hoop.
Class activity:
Students will practice shooting form at different distances around the basket, then participate in a modified basketball game focusing on proper technique.
Evaluation questions:
1. Describe the proper shooting technique in basketball.
2. What is traveling in basketball?
3. Name two basic skills in basketball besides shooting.
4. How is basketball similar to and different from football?
Summary:
Today we learned basketball shooting techniques and basic rules that govern the game.

topics.title: Ball games: volleyball
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate proper serving and spiking techniques, explain basic volleyball rules, and participate in a volleyball game.
Introduction:
Following football and basketball, we now learn volleyball skills which requires different techniques but similar teamwork and is played in many Nigerian schools.
Content:
Volleyball serving involves throwing the ball slightly above your head and hitting it with your hand over the net to the opponent's side. Spiking is hitting the ball forcefully downward into the opponent's court after receiving it. Basic rules include not catching the ball, hitting it a maximum of three times per side, and not touching the net. Like how market items are passed from hand to hand quickly, volleyball players must pass the ball efficiently. We practice serving first, then passing with forearms, before learning to spike. The game is played with two teams separated by a net.
Class activity:
Students will practice serving to partners and forearm passing drills, then participate in a simplified volleyball game focusing on proper technique.
Evaluation questions:
1. Describe the proper technique for a volleyball serve.
2. What is the maximum number of hits per team in volleyball?
3. Name two basic volleyball skills besides serving.
4. How is volleyball different from basketball in terms of ball handling?
Summary:
We have learned volleyball serving and spiking techniques along with basic rules that govern the game.

topics.title: Health: mental health
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to define mental health, identify signs of stress, and demonstrate relaxation techniques.
Introduction:
After physical activities, we now focus on mental health which is as important as physical health for overall wellbeing, especially during exam periods like BECE preparation.
Content:
Mental health is our emotional and psychological wellbeing. Signs of stress include feeling worried, having trouble sleeping, or getting angry easily. Common stressors for students include exams, family issues, and peer pressure. Coping strategies include talking to someone you trust, taking breaks to rest, and physical exercise. Harmattan season can sometimes affect our mood due to dry weather. Relaxation techniques include deep breathing (inhale slowly, hold, exhale slowly) and progressive muscle relaxation (tensing and relaxing different body parts). Like how we rest after a long day of farming, our minds also need regular rest.
Class activity:
Students will practice deep breathing and progressive muscle relaxation techniques while lying comfortably, then share how they felt during and after the exercise.
Evaluation questions:
1. Define mental health in your own words.
2. Name three signs of stress in students.
3. What are two coping strategies for stress?
4. How does the harmattan season sometimes affect our mental health?
Summary:
Today we learned about mental health, signs of stress, and relaxation techniques to maintain emotional wellbeing.

topics.title: Health: drugs in sport
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain why drugs are harmful in sports, identify common performance-enhancing drugs, and demonstrate commitment to fair play.
Introduction:
Building on our mental health discussion, today we address an important issue in sports: the use of drugs which undermines fair play and is against sports ethics in Nigeria and worldwide.
Content:
Drugs in sport refer to substances used to improve performance unfairly. Common examples include steroids, stimulants, and diuretics. These drugs can cause serious health problems like heart damage, liver failure, and mental health issues. They give an unfair advantage and violate the spirit of sportsmanship. Fair play means competing using only natural abilities and training. Like how examination cheating is wrong, using drugs in sports is dishonest. The World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) sets rules against doping in sports. We must say no to drugs and focus on natural training methods.
Class activity:
Students will create posters highlighting the dangers of drug use in sports and promoting fair play, to be displayed in the school.
Evaluation questions:
1. Why are performance-enhancing drugs harmful to health?
2. Name two examples of drugs used in sports.
3. What does fair play mean in sports?
4. How is using drugs in sports similar to examination cheating?
Summary:
We have learned about the dangers of drug use in sports and the importance of fair play and natural training.

topics.title: First aid: sports injuries
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify common sports injuries like sprains and cramps, demonstrate proper first aid techniques, and explain when to seek medical help.
Introduction:
In sports, injuries can happen like when children fall during play. Today we learn how to provide immediate help for common sports injuries like sprains and cramps.
Content:
A sprain is when ligaments around a joint are stretched or torn, often causing pain and swelling. First aid for sprains follows the RICE method: Rest (stop activity), Ice (apply cold compress), Compression (wrap with bandage), and Elevation (raise the injured part). A cramp is a sudden, painful muscle contraction often caused by dehydration or overexertion. To treat cramps, stretch the affected muscle gently and massage it. Prevention includes warming up properly and staying hydrated. Like how we preserve food to prevent spoilage, we take steps to prevent injuries. For serious injuries with severe pain or inability to move, we should seek medical help immediately.
Class activity:
Students will practice the RICE method on each other using bandages and ice packs for mock sprain injuries, and practice stretching techniques for muscle cramps.
Evaluation questions:
1. What is the RICE method for treating sprains?
2. What causes muscle cramps during sports?
3. Name two ways to prevent sports injuries.
4. When should you seek medical help for a sports injury?
Summary:
Today we learned first aid techniques for common sports injuries like sprains and cramps using the RICE method and proper stretching.

topics.title: Revision and BECE practice
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to answer past BECE questions correctly, identify areas needing further study, and demonstrate proper exam techniques.
Introduction:
As we approach the end of term and prepare for BECE, we will revise all topics covered and practice with past questions to build confidence for the examination.
Content:
We will review athletics skills including throws, jumps, and ball games like football, basketball, and volleyball. Health topics covered include mental health, drugs in sport, and first aid for sports injuries. We will practice with past BECE questions to understand the exam format and question types. Time management is important during exams, so we will practice answering questions within time limits. Like how traders prepare goods for market day, we prepare properly for our examination. We will mark and correct our answers together to learn from mistakes.
Class activity:
Students will work in groups to answer past BECE questions, then present their answers to the class for discussion and correction by the teacher.
Evaluation questions:
1. Name three topics covered in this term's physical and health education.
2. What is the RICE method for treating injuries?
3. Explain fair play in sports.
4. How do you prepare mentally for an examination?
Summary:
This week we revised all term's topics and practiced with past BECE questions to prepare for the upcoming examination.
